result: Higher frequency (≥19.5%) of CD44-/CD24- cells in breast cancer tissues is associated with delayed distant metastasis and worse disease-free survival (DFS) in the training cohort. ROC analysis established 19.5% as the optimal cutoff with 70.5% sensitivity and 71.2% specificity. Patients with high CD44-/CD24- frequency had 1.97-fold higher metastasis rates and significantly worse DFS across breast cancer subtypes (luminal, HER-2+, TNBC), with metastasis peaks occurring 5-7 years post-surgery.
evaluation: Claims C17-C21 and C66-C72 provide convergent evidence from ROC analysis (C18), metastasis rate comparisons (C19-C20), survival analysis (C68, C71-C72), and multivariate analysis (C21) demonstrating that CD44-/CD24- cell frequency predicts delayed metastasis. The 19.5% cutoff is statistically derived and validated across multiple breast cancer subtypes with consistent associations.

result: Validation in the testing cohort confirmed that higher CD44-/CD24- cell frequency predicts delayed metastasis and worse survival. Patients with high CD44-/CD24- frequency showed significantly shorter DFS and OS across molecular subtypes, with metastasis peaks at 4-5 years post-resection. This association persisted regardless of standard chemotherapy or endocrine therapy.
evaluation: Claims C73-C81 demonstrate independent validation of the training cohort findings in a separate patient population. The consistency of results across both cohorts, multiple breast cancer subtypes, and different treatment regimens strengthens the prognostic value of CD44-/CD24- cell frequency. Statistical significance is maintained across all comparisons.

result: CD44-/CD24- TNBC cells spontaneously convert into CD44+/CD24- cancer stem cells (CSCs) both in vitro and in vivo. After 7 days of culture, 4.6-28.3% of CD44-/CD24- cells converted to CSCs depending on culture conditions. In xenograft models, 10.8-16.3% of implanted CD44-/CD24- cells converted to CSCs at 7-21 days post-implantation.
evaluation: Claims C22-C24, C82-C83 provide direct experimental evidence of spontaneous conversion using flow cytometry in multiple experimental systems (primary human cells, cell lines, xenografts). The conversion rates are quantified and consistent across different time points and culture conditions, demonstrating reproducibility of the phenomenon.

result: Newly converted CD44+/CD24- CSCs from CD44-/CD24- cells exhibit functional properties indistinguishable from wild-type (WT) CSCs. Both cell types form similar numbers and sizes of mammospheres, display comparable proliferation rates, differentiate into similar cell subtypes, and express equivalent levels of stemness markers (OCT4, SOX2, NANOG, NESTIN, ABCB1).
evaluation: Claims C25-C28 and C84 demonstrate functional equivalence through multiple independent assays (mammosphere formation, proliferation, differentiation, protein expression). The comprehensive characterization across multiple stemness properties provides strong evidence that converted CSCs are functionally equivalent to WT CSCs.

result: Both WT CSCs and newly converted CD44+/CD24- CSCs demonstrate equivalent tumorigenicity and metastatic capacity in vivo. Equal numbers of each CSC type induced xenograft tumors of similar sizes and weights after 21 days, and produced comparable lung metastatic nodules with similar tumor sizes and lung weights in NOD/SCID mice.
evaluation: Claims C29-C30 and C85 provide in vivo validation that converted CSCs have equivalent tumorigenic and metastatic properties to WT CSCs. The use of equal cell numbers, multiple endpoints (tumor size, weight, metastatic nodules), and appropriate mouse models strengthens the conclusion of functional equivalence.

result: RNA-seq analysis of single cells during CD44-/CD24- to CSC conversion identified 11 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including RHBDL2, HIST1H4H, and PPME1. These genes showed >2-fold upregulation in converted CSCs compared to unconverted cells. Higher expression of RHBDL2, HIST1H4H, DSCC1, ARL6IP1, and PPME1 was associated with worse DFS in TCGA breast cancer patients.
evaluation: Claims C31-C34, C64, C86-C87 describe a systematic approach to identify molecular drivers of conversion using single-cell RNA-seq. The validation in TCGA data (C33) and RT-qPCR confirmation (C34) strengthen the findings. GO/KEGG analyses (C86) provide biological context for the DEGs.

result: RHBDL2 silencing inhibits spontaneous CD44-/CD24- to CSC conversion and reduces mammosphere formation. RHBDL2 knockdown decreased YAP1 expression, increased YAP1 phosphorylation and USP31 expression, reduced nuclear YAP1 translocation, decreased NF-κB phosphorylation, and reduced CSC conversion from 6.5-5.5% to 0.5-0.7% in TNBC cells.
evaluation: Claims C35-C39, C60, C65 demonstrate a clear mechanistic link between RHBDL2 and CSC conversion through loss-of-function experiments. Multiple signaling components (YAP1, USP31, NF-κB) are examined with Western blot and subcellular fractionation, and functional outcomes (CSC conversion, mammosphere formation) are quantified, providing comprehensive mechanistic evidence.

result: RHBDL2 regulates spontaneous CD44-/CD24- to CSC conversion through the YAP1/USP31/NF-κB signaling axis. RHBDL2 enhances YAP1 stability by inhibiting its phosphorylation, which suppresses USP31 expression (a potent NF-κB inhibitor), thereby enhancing NF-κB signaling to promote CSC conversion.
evaluation: Claims C41, C55, C61, C88 synthesize the mechanistic findings into a coherent signaling pathway. The proposed mechanism is supported by the RHBDL2 silencing experiments (C35-C39) showing coordinated changes in all pathway components. The pathway is consistent with established YAP1/USP31/NF-κB biology (C88, C92).

result: Higher frequency of CD44-/CD24- cells predicts delayed distant metastasis (5-7 years post-diagnosis) particularly in patients with low CSC frequency, and CD44-/CD24- cell frequency may serve as a prognostic biomarker for breast cancer, especially TNBC. The spontaneous conversion of CD44-/CD24- cells to CSCs helps maintain the CSC pool, contributing to delayed metastasis and worse prognosis.
evaluation: Claims C40, C42, C48, C58, C62, C80, C89 integrate the clinical and mechanistic findings to propose CD44-/CD24- frequency as a prognostic biomarker. The claims are supported by the clinical validation data (training and testing cohorts) and the mechanistic studies demonstrating conversion to CSCs. The temporal pattern of delayed metastasis is consistent across multiple analyses.

result: Breast cancer is the most prevalent malignancy in women with increasing global incidence. While various treatment strategies have improved survival, delayed metastasis occurring 5-40 years after diagnosis remains a significant clinical challenge causing cancer relapse and poor survival.
evaluation: Claims C1-C5 establish the clinical context through citations to published literature. These background claims are well-supported by multiple references and provide the rationale for studying delayed metastasis.

result: Tumor metastasis is a multistep process with colonization as the rate-limiting step. CD44+/CD24- breast CSCs are associated with distant metastasis, display high motility/invasiveness, are chemoresistant, and can be replenished through spontaneous conversion of differentiated cancer cells, contributing to TNBC relapse.
evaluation: Claims C6-C14 provide established biological context about metastasis and CSCs through citations to published literature. These claims establish the scientific foundation for investigating CD44-/CD24- cell conversion to CSCs.

result: Non-CSC tumor cells can dedifferentiate into CSCs in multiple cancer types, contributing to intra-tumoral heterogeneity. CSC plasticity and heterogeneity promote tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and are major challenges for effective cancer therapy.
evaluation: Claims C43-C47 provide literature-based context about CSC plasticity and its clinical implications. These claims are well-supported by citations and establish the broader significance of studying CSC conversion.

result: RHBDL2 is an intramembrane serine protease that cleaves multiple substrates (EGF, ephrin-β3, thrombomodulin, CLEC14A, cadherin, IL-6R, Spint-1, DDR1), activates EGF signaling and angiogenesis, promotes cell migration, and its upregulation is associated with worse prognosis in multiple cancer types including breast cancer.
evaluation: Claims C49-C52 provide established knowledge about RHBDL2 through citations to published literature. This background establishes RHBDL2 as a relevant candidate for mechanistic investigation.

result: YAP1 enhances CSC stemness in multiple cancers, and aberrant YAP1 activation is associated with poor TNBC differentiation and survival. Upregulated RHBDL2 expression is associated with worse DFS in TCGA breast cancer patients. YAP1-mediated suppression of USP31 enhances NF-κB activity to promote sarcomagenesis.
evaluation: Claims C53-C54, C91-C92 provide literature-based context about YAP1 signaling and validate RHBDL2's clinical relevance using TCGA data. These claims support the rationale for investigating the RHBDL2/YAP1/USP31/NF-κB axis.

result: The study collected paraffin-embedded surgical tissue samples from 576 breast cancer patients who underwent surgery between June 2005 and April 2013 at three medical centers in China.
evaluation: Claim C16 describes the study design and sample collection. This methodological detail is clearly stated and provides the basis for the clinical analyses.

result: The study hypothesizes that CD44-/CD24- cell frequency may predict delayed metastasis, RHBDL2 may cleave other substrates to activate EGF signaling and promote conversion, RHBDL2 may be a therapeutic target, and CD44-/CD24- cells may convert to CSCs through clonal evolution driven by environmental factors and mutations.
evaluation: Claims C15, C56, C57, C90 are explicitly speculative or hypothetical. While C15 is validated by subsequent experiments, C56-C57 and C90 propose mechanisms and applications that require additional experimental validation beyond the current study.

result: Summary claims stating that CD44-/CD24- cells spontaneously convert to CSCs with similar stemness properties in vitro and in vivo, encompassing stemness marker expression, self-renewal, differentiation, tumorigenicity, and lung metastasis.
evaluation: Claims C59 and C63 are summary statements that synthesize multiple experimental findings already evaluated in other result groups. These claims are supported by the comprehensive experimental evidence from C22-C30 and related claims.
